title: Restriction preserves vanishing of ideal-power products
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $K$ a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-ideal-zero-set-affine], $F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], $V$ an open subset of $X$, and $n\geq 0$. Form $K^nF$ as the image of multiplication, with $K^0=\mathcal O_X$ and identity inclusion [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-module-product-stalk]. Write $K|_V$ for the comap ideal and $F|_V$ for restriction [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits]. Then $(K^nF)|_V=0$ if and only if $(K|_V)^n(F|_V)=0$, where zero means a zero object in the category of module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

source.place: Tag 01YD, lemma-prepare-filter-support, proof: restriction of I^n F to X minus Z'; with Schemes Tag 01I8 and Modules Tag 01CD. Read online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01YD.

proof.text: Restriction computes sections on image opens with scalars transported through the structure-ring isomorphism. Kernels are computed sectionwise, so restriction preserves kernels; the restriction adjunction preserves cokernels. Consequently restriction preserves images. The natural tensor and unit comparisons identify the multiplication maps, since on pure tensors both composites give a scalar times a section.

The restriction of the inclusion of K agrees with the inclusion of its comap to V: check the section ideals on each affine open of V. The product restriction comparison identifies the resulting multiplication images as subobjects.

Induct on n to identify the restricted power inclusion with the power of the restricted inclusion. At zero both are identity inclusions of the structure sheaf. At one use the preceding identification. At n+2 use the multiplication-image comparison on K and its (n+1)-st power and compose their inclusions. Apply that comparison to the product with F.

The preceding identifications yield an isomorphism of the two module sheaves. Being a zero object is invariant under isomorphism, proving both directions. This includes n=0, the empty open, the zero module and the zero and unit ideals.

lean.statement:
theorem idealPowerProduct_restrict_isZero_iff {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (K : X.IdealSheafData) (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent]
    (V : X.Opens) (n : ℕ) :
    IsZero ((restrictFunctor V.ι).obj
      (idealModuleProduct (idealSheafPower K.toModulesι n).2 F)) ↔
    IsZero (idealModuleProduct (idealSheafPower (K.comap V.ι).toModulesι n).2
      ((restrictFunctor V.ι).obj F))
